Import the data

billboard <- read_csv("billboard.csv", 
                           col_types = cols(
                            url = col_skip(), 
                            song = col_skip(),
                            instance = col_skip()
                            ))
print(head(billboard,5))
audio_features <- read_csv("audio_features.csv", 
                          col_types = cols( 
                            performer = col_skip(), 
                            song = col_skip(), 
                            spotify_track_preview_url = col_skip(),
                            spotify_track_explicit = col_skip(),
                            spotify_track_album = col_skip(),
                            spotify_track_id = col_skip()
                            ))
print(head(audio_features,5))
billboard <- na.omit(billboard) # remove all NaN
audio_features <- as_tibble(audio_features) # translate in a modern and more flexible version
audio_features <- na.omit(audio_features) # remove all NaN

full_data <- left_join(billboard, audio_features, by = "song_id") # merge datasets

Question 1 - Given the audio features of a new song, in which position it will chart on Billboard?

Regression - predict the position on the Billboard

One hot encoding of the 15 most frequent genre

regression_data_encoded <- process_and_encode_genre(regression_data, top_n = 15)

Regression


set.seed(45)
split <- initial_split(regression_data_encoded, prop = 0.8)
train_data <- training(split)
test_data  <- testing(split)

# recipe
#recipe_spec <- recipe(spotify_track_popularity ~ ., data = train_data)
recipe_spec <- recipe(spotify_track_popularity ~ ., data = train_data) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE)

# define models
task = 'regression'

models <- list(
  rf = rand_forest(mtry = 5) %>% set_engine("randomForest") %>% set_mode(task),
  #lm = linear_reg() %>% set_engine("lm") %>% set_mode(task),
  xgb = boost_tree(trees = 1000, tree_depth = 10) %>% set_engine("xgboost") %>% set_mode(task),
  knn = nearest_neighbor(neighbors = 5) %>% set_engine("kknn") %>% set_mode(task)
)

# workflow list
workflows_list <- purrr::map(models, ~ workflow() %>% add_model(.x) %>% add_recipe(recipe_spec))

# train the models
fitted_models <- purrr::map(workflows_list, ~ fit(.x, data = train_data))

# evaluation
results <- purrr::map(fitted_models, ~ {
  predict(.x, test_data) %>%
    bind_cols(test_data) %>%
    metrics(truth = spotify_track_popularity, estimate = .pred)
})

# Results
results_df <- bind_rows(results, .id = "model")

results_df %>%
  filter(.metric == "rmse") %>%
  arrange(.estimate)

print(results_df)
results <- list()

for (model_name in names(fitted_models)) {
  model <- models[[model_name]]
  
  wf <- workflow() %>%
    add_model(model) %>%
    add_recipe(recipe_spec)
  
  fit_model <- fit(wf, data = train_data)
  
  preds <- predict(fit_model, test_data) %>%
    bind_cols(test_data) %>%
    mutate(model = model_name)
  
  results[[model_name]] <- preds
}

all_predictions <- bind_rows(results)


ggplot(all_predictions, aes(x = spotify_track_popularity, y = .pred)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~model, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    title = "Predictions vs Real Values",
    x = "Real Values (spotify_track_popularity)",
    y = "Predictions"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# VIP plot list
vip_plots <- list()

# Random Forest
rf_fit <- extract_fit_parsnip(fitted_models$rf)
if (inherits(rf_fit$fit, "randomForest")) {
  vip_plots$rf <- vip(rf_fit$fit, num_features = 15) + ggtitle("Random Forest - Variable Importance")
}

# XGBoost
xgb_fit <- extract_fit_parsnip(fitted_models$xgb)
if (inherits(xgb_fit$fit, "xgb.Booster")) {
  vip_plots$xgb <- vip(xgb_fit$fit, num_features = 15) + ggtitle("XGBoost - Variable Importance")
}

# visualize plots
library(patchwork)

Random forest

Question 2 - As a manager, should I continue to invest in this song given its statistics? Will it remain popular over time?

Regression - predict the position on the Billboard

Preprocessing

Remove unrelevant features

regression_data <- full_data_aggregate %>% select(-c(song_id))
print(head(regression_data,5))
# removes useless not required characters
regression_data$spotify_genre <- gsub("\\[|\\]|'", "", regression_data$spotify_genre)
# create a list, with div = ,
regression_data$spotify_genre <- strsplit(regression_data$spotify_genre, split = ",")
# extract only the first genre for each line
regression_data$first_genre <- sapply(regression_data$spotify_genre, function(x) x[1])

regression_data$first_genre <- sapply(regression_data$spotify_genre, function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0) {
    return("others")
  } else {
    return(x[1])
  }
})

# frequency counter
genre_counts <- table(regression_data$first_genre)

# order based in descrescent order the frequency
genre_counts_sorted <- sort(genre_counts, decreasing = TRUE)

# take only first 15 genres
top_15_genres <- names(genre_counts_sorted)[1:15]

# named others as "others"
regression_data$first_genre <- ifelse(
  regression_data$first_genre %in% top_15_genres,
  regression_data$first_genre,
  "others"
)
print(head(regression_data,5))

# verify
genre_counts_after_grouping <- table(regression_data$first_genre)

# drop original spotify_genre column
regression_data <- subset(regression_data, select = -c(spotify_genre))

# ensure the column is upgraded for dummyVars
df <- data.frame(first_genre = regression_data$first_genre)

# create dummy variables (one-hot encoding)
dummy <- dummyVars(~ first_genre, data = df)
final_df <- data.frame(predict(dummy, newdata = df))

# bind dummy variables to the rest of regression_data (without first_genre)
regression_data_encoded <- bind_cols(
  regression_data %>% select(-first_genre),
  final_df
)

print(head(regression_data_encoded, 5))

Regression


set.seed(45)
split <- initial_split(regression_data_encoded, prop = 0.8)
train_data <- training(split)
test_data  <- testing(split)

# 1. Prepara il recipe (già fatto)
#recipe_spec <- recipe(spotify_track_popularity ~ ., data = train_data)
recipe_spec <- recipe(final_position ~ ., data = train_data) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors(), one_hot = TRUE)

task = 'regression'

# 2. Definisci i modelli
models <- list(
  rf = rand_forest(mtry = 5) %>% set_engine("randomForest") %>% set_mode(task),
  #lm = linear_reg() %>% set_engine("lm") %>% set_mode(task),
  xgb = boost_tree(trees = 1000, tree_depth = 10) %>% set_engine("xgboost") %>% set_mode(task),
  knn = nearest_neighbor(neighbors = 5) %>% set_engine("kknn") %>% set_mode(task)
)

# 3. Crea una lista di workflow
workflows_list <- purrr::map(models, ~ workflow() %>% add_model(.x) %>% add_recipe(recipe_spec))

# 4. Fitta tutti i modelli
fitted_models <- purrr::map(workflows_list, ~ fit(.x, data = train_data))

# 5. Valuta su test set
results <- purrr::map(fitted_models, ~ {
  predict(.x, test_data) %>%
    bind_cols(test_data) %>%
    metrics(truth = final_position, estimate = .pred)
})

# 6. Combina risultati in una tabella leggibile
results_df <- bind_rows(results, .id = "model")

results_df %>%
  filter(.metric == "rmse") %>%
  arrange(.estimate)

print(results_df)
results <- list()

for (model_name in names(fitted_models)) {
  model <- models[[model_name]]
  
  wf <- workflow() %>%
    add_model(model) %>%
    add_recipe(recipe_spec)
  
  fit_model <- fit(wf, data = train_data)
  
  preds <- predict(fit_model, test_data) %>%
    bind_cols(test_data) %>%
    mutate(model = model_name)
  
  results[[model_name]] <- preds
}

# Unione di tutte le predizioni
all_predictions <- bind_rows(results)


ggplot(all_predictions, aes(x = final_position, y = .pred)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~model, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    title = "Predizioni vs Valori Reali per Modello",
    x = "Valori Reali (spotify_track_popularity)",
    y = "Predizioni"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

Classification- predict whether a sogn will be in the top 10

Preprocessing

classification_data <- full_data_aggregate %>% select(-c( song_id, final_position))
print(head(classification_data,5))
#create the new variable top10: whether a song is in the top 30
classification_data <- classification_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(spotify_track_popularity)) 

classification_data <- classification_data %>%
  mutate(top30 = ifelse(avg_position <= 30, 1, 0))

# encode popularity
classification_data$spotify_track_popularity <- sapply(classification_data$spotify_track_popularity, function(x) {
  if (x <= 25) {
    return("low")
  }
  if (x > 25 & x <= 50) {
    return("medium")
  }
  if (x > 50 & x <= 75) {
    return("high")
  }
    if (x > 75 & x <= 100) {
    return("very high")
  } 
})
#remove useless features (usefull only)
classification_data <- classification_data %>% select(-c( avg_position, min_position, max_position))
# Step 1: Rimuovi caratteri indesiderati
classification_data$spotify_genre <- gsub("\\[|\\]|'", "", classification_data$spotify_genre)

# Step 2: Creare una lista di generi separati da virgola
classification_data$spotify_genre <- strsplit(classification_data$spotify_genre, split = ",")

# Step 3: Estrarre solo il primo genere per ogni riga
classification_data$first_genre <- sapply(classification_data$spotify_genre, function(x) x[1])

classification_data$first_genre <- sapply(classification_data$spotify_genre, function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0) {
    return("others")
    } else {
    return(x[1])
  }
})

# frequency counter
genre_counts <- table(classification_data$first_genre)

# order based in descrescent order the frequency
genre_counts_sorted <- sort(genre_counts, decreasing = TRUE)

# take only first 15 genres
top_15_genres <- names(genre_counts_sorted)[1:15]

# named others as "others"
classification_data$first_genre <- ifelse(
  classification_data$first_genre %in% top_15_genres,
  classification_data$first_genre,
  "others"
)

# verify
genre_counts_after_grouping <- table(classification_data$first_genre)

# drop original spotify_genre column
classification_data <- subset(classification_data, select = -c(spotify_genre))

df <- data.frame(first_genre = classification_data$first_genre)

# create dummy variables (one-hot encoding)
dummy <- dummyVars(~ first_genre, data = df)
final_df <- data.frame(predict(dummy, newdata = df))

# bind dummy variables to the rest of regression_data (without first_genre)
